Date October 21, 19 37.

Subject Kuo Mo-ju (郭沫若), left-wing writer.

Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Gaudin

with reference to the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch)
appended to the attached report, I beg to submit hereunder
the brief antecedents of Mr. Kuo Mo-ju, a left-wing writer,
and an ex-communist.

Mr. Kuo, age about 50, is a native of Szechuen, known as
the fighting poet and novelist and well known for his transla-
tion of the German work of Goeth's "Die Leiden des Jungen Werthers."

From the age of 22-26, he received part of his education
in Japan, and in 1925-1926, was appointed Dean of the College
of Arts of the Chungshan University, Canton. The principal
on learning of his communist tendencies dismissed him in the sum-
mer of 1926. He then joined the Political Department of the
Field Headquarters of the North Punitive Expedition Forces as
Chief of the Propaganda Section, Gen. Chiang Kai Shek being
Commander of the Forces, and Teng Yen-tah (邓演达), Chief of
the Political Department. Teng Yen-tah later became leader
of the "Third Party," (第三党) and was arrested on 17/8/31
in Shanghai and executed in winter of the same year in Nanking.

In October, 1926, Mr. Kuo was promoted to Vice Chief of
the Political Department in which the Communists had gradually
obtained a place of prominence.

At the beginning of 1927 he secured also the post of
Chief of the Political Department of the 2nd Army Group, of
which Gen. Chang Fah Kwei (张发奎), the present officer com-
manding the troops in Footung, was the Commander. It was
reported that the Communist Party were the means of securing
that position for Mr. Kuo and he joined the Party the same year.

报告
日期：1937年10月21日。

主题：郭沫若（Kuo Mo-ju），左翼作家。

制作人：职员廖仲坚（Liao Chung Chien） 转呈人：C. Gaudin

参照附呈报告后所附特务科副主管（D.C.）的评语，谨此提交左翼作家、前共产党员郭沫若先生的简要履历。

郭先生，年约五十，四川人，被称为“战斗诗人”及小说家，并因翻译德国歌德（Goethe）的作品《少年维特之烦恼》（Die Leiden des Jungen Werthers）而闻名。

22岁至26岁期间，他在日本接受部分教育；1925年至1926年间，被任命为广州中山大学文学院院长。校长获悉其共产主义倾向后，于1926年夏季将其解职。随后，他加入北伐军野战司令部政治部，担任宣传科科长，当时部队总司令为蒋介石将军，政治部主任为邓演达（Teng Yen-tah）。邓演达后来成为“第三党”领袖，于1931年8月17日在上海被捕，并于同年冬季在南京被处决。

1926年10月，郭先生升任政治部副主任，此时共产党人在该部门已逐渐占据显要地位。

1927年初，他还获得了第二集团军政治部主任一职，该集团军司令为现任浦东部队指挥官张发奎（Chang Fah Kwei）将军。据报，共产党方面促成了郭先生获得该职位，他亦于同年入党。

值得注意的是，当时的政治部被视为军队的监督机构，且

（左侧手写批注：）

未来活动

obliged to consult the chiefs of the political departments of
their respective units before taking any military action.
This system still functions in the red armies of the present
day.
In July 1927, the Wuhan Government adopted very drastic
measures in an endeavour to purge the army of the communist
menace. In retaliation, the Communist elements incited the
1st Division of the 9th North Expedition Army under Gen. Ho
Lung (贺龙), and the Independent Regiment of the 4th Route
Gen.
Army under Yih T'ing (叶挺) to revolt. The rebelling troops
staged a riot in Nanchang, the capital of Kiangsi Province,
at the end of 1927, and established a Soviet style government
in that city which was under the control of a Revolutionary
Committee (革命委员会) consisting of Mr. Kuo Mo-ju and the
following five prominent communists:-
Tan Ping San (谭平山), Chief director of the activities
of the Communist Party among the working classes.
Kao Yu Han (高语罕), a native of Anhwei, returned
student from Germany, very active in the May 30th
Incident Movement in 1925 in Shanghai.
Yuin Dai Ying (恽代英), arrested and executed by the
Nanking Government in 1930.
Ling Tsu Han (林祖涵), a native of Hunan, an active
member in the Propaganda Dept. of the Communist Party.
Wu Yu Tsang (吴玉章), a native of Szechuen, returned
student from France, President of the Sino-Franco
University in Szechuen in the year 1925.

在许多北伐军中，指挥官在采取任何军事行动前，必须征询各自单位政治部主任的意见。
这一制度在当今的红军中仍然运作。
1927年7月，武汉政府采取严厉措施，试图清除军队中的共产主义威胁。作为报复，共产主义分子煽动贺龙（Ho Lung）将军率领的北伐第九军第一师，以及叶挺（Yih T'ing）将军率领的第四路军独立团发动叛变。叛军于1927年底在江西省会南昌发动暴动，并在该市建立了苏维埃式政府，该政府由一个革命委员会控制，成员包括郭沫若先生以及以下五位著名共产党员：
谭平山（Tan Ping San），共产党在工人阶级中活动的主任。
高语罕（Kao Yu Han），安徽人，留德归国学生，在1925年上海五卅运动期间非常活跃。
恽代英（Yuin Dai Ying），1930年被南京政府逮捕并处决。
林祖涵（Ling Tsu Han），湖南人，共产党宣传部活跃成员。
吴玉章（Wu Yu Tsang），四川人，留法归国学生，1925年任四川中法大学校长。

in order to avoid being trapped by the National Government
forces, withdrew from Nanchang shortly afterwards and resorted
to guerilla warfare on borders of Kiangsi, Fokien and Kwangtung
provinces. Mr. Kuo followed these red troops in their retreat
and at the beginning of 1928 they met a crushing defeat in
Kwangtung Province. Mr. Kuo fled to Shanghai, and in the
Spring of 1928 he left for Japan, where he stayed up to the end
of July, 1937, when the order issued by the National Government
in 1927 for his arrest was cancelled, and he returned to China
arriving in Shanghai at the beginning of August, 1937. His
wife, a Japanese, and two sons, born of the union, are at
present in Japan. It is reported that Mr. Kuo was expelled
from the membership of the Communist Party in 1933 for leading
a "romantic" life in Japan.
    On his return, Mr. Kuo is reported to have visited Nanking
and interviewed Gen. Chiang Kai Shek, and although he has not
been given a definite position in the Government it is known
that he received instructions to conduct propaganda in Shanghai
in favour of the war of resistance against Japan. At present
he writes articles for various local vernacular papers and
magazines and has often participated in meetings convened by
local national salvation bodies, but enquiries have, however,
failed to show that he has any direct connection with the
Alleyway Tenants' Associations, which were promoted by the
Citizens' Federations.
                                                Liao Chungchin.

为避免被国民政府军队包围，不久后便撤离南昌，转而在江西、福建和广东三省边境开展游击战。郭先生跟随这些红色部队撤退，1928年初，他们在广东省遭受惨败。郭先生逃往上海，并于1928年春前往日本，在那里一直居住到1937年7月底，此时国民政府于1927年发布的对他的逮捕令被撤销，他随即返回中国，于1937年8月初抵达上海。他的妻子是日本人，两人育有两子，目前均在日本。据报，郭先生因在日本过着“浪漫”生活，于1933年被开除出共产党。
据报，回国后，郭先生曾访问南京并面见蒋介石将军，虽然未在政府中获得明确职位，但据悉他受命在上海进行有利于抗日战争的宣传工作。目前，他为当地各种白话报纸和杂志撰写文章，并经常参加由当地救国会召开的会议，但经查询，未发现他与市民联合会 promoted 的里弄租户协会有任何直接联系。
                                                廖仲坚（Liao Chungchin）。
